title: Study notes
html:
Which method for which woman

  • Mammography (CC + MLO): screening from 40–50 years, the only method that reliably shows microcalcifications; limited in dense breasts.
  • Ultrasound: < 35 years, pregnancy/lactation, dense breasts, palpable lump, cyst vs solid, axillary nodes, guidance for biopsy.
  • MRI: high-risk screening (BRCA), implants, extent of known cancer, multifocality, response to chemotherapy, occult primary.

Benign or malignant?

BenignMalignant
Shape / marginsOval, circumscribedIrregular, spiculated, angular, indistinct
Orientation (US)Parallel to skin ("wider than tall")Not parallel ("taller than wide")
Behind the lesion (US)Enhancement (cyst)Shadowing
CalcificationsCoarse popcorn (fibroadenoma), rim, vascularFine pleomorphic, linear branching, segmental clusters
Around itNothingArchitectural distortion, skin thickening/retraction, nipple retraction, axillary nodes

BI-RADS – what to do

0 incomplete → more imaging · 1 negative · 2 benign · 3 probably benign → follow-up in 6 months · 4 suspicious → biopsy · 5 highly suggestive → biopsy · 6 proven cancer → treatment.

Exam reflexes

  • BI-RADS 6 does not need a biopsy – it already had one.
  • Ultrasound is not only for suspicion of malignancy.
